missing.behaviour: Phase allocation when totalWeeks does not equal the sum of progressionRules weeks (targetDate-driven lengths, e.g. 30 weeks for a 5k whose rules total ~10): counts must be rebalanced to exactly totalWeeks and phases array length must equal totalWeeks.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: The redistribution loop produces fewer entries than totalWeeks, so phases[w] is undefined; volumeCurve then falls back to a default rule and weeks get an undefined/wrong phase (crash or silently wrong plan). Only a base->taper smoke case is tested today.
The over-volume branch is inverted or its thresholds wrong, so a runner ramping 30%+ per week gets no warning (injury risk). Only the under-volume path is tested.

missing.behaviour: Round-trip sign then verify returns the payload; verify rejects a tampered token, a token signed with a different secret, and an expired token; sessionKey throws when SESSION_SECRET is shorter than 32 bytes.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: A forged or expired session cookie is accepted (auth bypass), or the secret-length guard is dropped so a weak/empty SESSION_SECRET is silently used to sign sessions.

missing.behaviour: Nonce mismatch is rejected and identity mapping enforces emailVerified; identityFromClaims maps sub/email/name/picture.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: OIDC id_token replay is accepted (nonce not enforced) or an unverified email is trusted, enabling account takeover.

missing.behaviour: deload weeks (rule.deload && (idx+1)%4===0) step to 0.7x; taper weeks step down monotonically from the peak.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: The deload condition is inverted or applied every week, so volume climbs unchecked through build (overtraining) or the plan collapses; the taper becomes non-monotonic so it does not freshen the runner.

missing.behaviour: When baseline.weeklyKm is absent, base volume derives from experience (beginner 0.55 / intermediate 1 / advanced 1.5) and profile factor.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: A beginner is handed advanced-tier weekly volume (or vice versa) because the experience factor table regressed; only whole-fitness/beginner is exercised indirectly.

missing.behaviour: Goal pace per profile: marathon=marathon pace, half=(marathon+threshold)/2, 10k=threshold, 5k=(threshold+interval)/2.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: Race-pace targets are computed from the wrong anchor (e.g. 10k goal pace not threshold), so race-pace workouts and targetPaceSecPerKm are wrong.

missing.behaviour: Spike compares a run against the max distance in the trailing 30-day window (not all-time).
missing.failure_it_would_catch: The window is wrong (all-time or unbounded), so normal progressive long runs are flagged as spikes, or genuine >10% jumps are missed.

missing.behaviour: Volume feedback uses the most recent completed week that has actual volume > 0, not simply the last plan week.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: A zero-volume week short-circuits the volume check, so the runner never gets hold/rebuild/back-off guidance after a skipped week.

missing.behaviour: Fixed-window counter increments within a window and resets to 1 once now - window_start >= windowSec; ok is count <= limit.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: The window never resets (permanent lockout after the limit) or always resets (no effective limiting), from a regression in the CASE expression.

missing.behaviour: cacheKey is deterministic: identical {type,model,input} yields the same key; different input yields a different key.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: Non-deterministic or colliding cache keys, so AI answers are re-billed on every request or a stale response is served for different input.

missing.behaviour: extractJsonArray pulls a JSON array out of noisy model text and returns null when the array length does not match weeks.length; templateWeekSummary is the deterministic fallback.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: Model prose containing brackets is misparsed, or a partial array is accepted, so weekly summaries are misaligned to the wrong weeks or an unusable string is persisted.

missing.behaviour: chunk splits inserts into batches under D1's 100 bound-parameter cap (weeks of 10, sessions of 8).
missing.failure_it_would_catch: A larger batch exceeds D1's bound-parameter limit, so plan generation 500s on longer plans.

missing.behaviour: State-changing requests are rejected unless Origin is in the WEB_ORIGIN/APP_ORIGIN allowlist (plus localhost in non-production); safe methods pass through.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: A wrong allowlist lets cross-origin POST/PUT/DELETE through (CSRF), or blocks legitimate same-origin writes.

missing.behaviour: JSON-mode columns round-trip their objects and user_goals delete cascades to plans -> plan_weeks -> sessions_plan (account deletion leaves no orphans).
missing.failure_it_would_catch: A migration drifts the JSON/timestamp serialization or drops a cascade, so account deletion leaves orphaned plan/session rows (leaked data), which AGENTS.md names as in-scope.

missing.behaviour: parseClaims parses '### topic' blocks from the assembled full text into topic/claim/evidence/confidence/source.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: Malformed KB full text yields dropped or mis-attributed claims shown to the user as research evidence.

missing.behaviour: Coach context picks the week whose start/end brackets today, else falls back to the first week.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: The wrong week is chosen (e.g. off-by-one on date comparison), so coach replies reference the wrong sessions.

missing.behaviour: formatClock renders 'h:mm:ss' once total seconds reach one hour.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: A duration >= 1h renders as '75:00' instead of '1:15:00'.

missing.behaviour: parseTime returns undefined for non-numeric parts (and a sane value for empty/garbage), and formatPace carries a rounded 60 seconds into the minute.
missing.failure_it_would_catch: formatPace(299.6) renders '4:60' (no carry), and a garbage time string is parsed as 0, so a bogus VDOT could be derived from baseline times. Note: this formatPace export is currently unused by the app (web uses units.formatPace).

violations.issue: Asserts the identity/metric branch and the conversion constant directly rather than user-visible output: expect(convertPace(300,'metric')).toBe(300) and the kmToMiles/milesToKm/pacePerKmToPerMile assertions mirror the implementation (they restate KM_PER_MILE and the formula). The formatPace/formatDistance/formatPaceBand assertions in the same file do carry real value.
violations.recommendation: Drop the identity-branch and raw-formula assertions; keep the formatting assertions that protect displayed strings.

violations.issue: The 'labels every session easy / steady / hard' test only asserts membership in a 3-value enum and is near-trivial; it largely duplicates 'maps archetypes to the expected band' (lines 109-115).
violations.recommendation: Replace with the specific archetype->band mapping that matters (e.g. tempo/threshold->steady, race->hard) or fold into the existing mapping test.

violations.issue: Borderline: the pace-ordering test asserts the anchor ordering rather than a computed user-facing pace. It encodes a genuine invariant (harder work is faster), so it is acceptable, but it is close to mirroring the anchors.
violations.recommendation: Optionally assert an absolute pace value for a known VDOT to pin the anchors, or leave as-is.

summary: 5 test files, all in packages/shared (346 lines); apps/api has no test script or runner at all, so the whole API layer is untested. Well covered: engine smoke/phase/volume-shape invariants, VDOT sanity + pace ordering, units formatting, adapt happy paths, analytics aggregation. Highest-value gaps: phaseSequence when totalWeeks != sum of rule weeks (undefined phase/crash), the untested volume-over adaptive rule (injury risk), and the entire auth/session/rate-limit security surface (session forgery/expiry, OIDC nonce, rate-limit window reset). Medium gaps cluster on plan-engine branch logic (deload, taper monotonicity, baseWeeklyKm, goalPaceFor), adapt windows, and API helpers (cache key, narration JSON extraction, plans chunking, CSRF origin check, schema cascades). Violations are minor: a few unit assertions mirror the implementation and one engine test is a near-trivial enum-membership check.
